# Adapter catalogue

Every adapter that connects a device, a recording file, a public dataset or a decoder to Fidetype, with its status and licence.

**Status:** Alpha ([status levels](glossary.md#status-levels))

<!-- Generated by `python -m fidetype.adapters.registry` from the ADAPTER_INFO of each adapter module and
     src/fidetype/adapters/planned.py. Do not edit by hand. CI fails when this page is stale. -->

An **adapter** connects a device, a recording file, a public dataset or a decoder to Fidetype. This page lists every adapter in the repository and the adapters that we plan. The machine-readable registry is [adapters.json](adapters.json) (schema `fidetype.adapter-registry/0.2`).

**Counts:** 16 tested, 1 experimental, 16 planned. **No adapter is tested on a real device yet** (column "Real device"). Real-device tests need hardware and volunteers, so they wait on outside help.

Which device, file format or dataset works, on what data each one ran and its known limits: [device support matrix](device-support.md) (generated from the same metadata).

To add an adapter, read [CONTRIBUTING.md, section 7](../CONTRIBUTING.md#7-adapters-add-a-decoder-or-a-device). The template is in [templates/adapter/](../templates/adapter/).

## Status

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tested` | CI tests run it, and it ran on the real thing it reads: real public dataset files, or the real protocol library (pylsl, websockets, BrainFlow) in a loopback. |
| `experimental` | Code and CI tests on synthetic data exist. It has not run on real recordings or a real device. |
| `planned` | No code yet. Not supported. |

## Kinds

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dataset-replay` | reads a public dataset and emits NTS streams |
| `dataset-reader` | reads the raw files of a public dataset |
| `decoder-output` | turns the output of any decoder into NTS |
| `transport` | moves NTS between programs (network) |
| `device-source` | reads a live device (signal source) |
| `file-reader` | reads a recording file format (signal source) |
| `synthetic-source` | makes synthetic signals (no real data) |

## File readers for `fidetype live`

`fidetype live --source file --path FILE` picks the reader whose file-name pattern matches FILE (case-insensitive). `--reader ID` picks a reader by its id (for a renamed file, or when more than one pattern matches). See [live-decode.md, section 3a](live-decode.md#3a-recording-files---source-file).

| Id | File names | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `edf` | `*.edf`, `*.bdf` | `fidetype live --source file --reader edf --path FILE` |
| `openbci-gui` | `OpenBCI-RAW-*.txt`, `OpenBCI_GUI-*.txt` | `fidetype live --source file --reader openbci-gui --path FILE` |

## Details of adapters without their own page

### edf

Module `fidetype.adapters.edf`.

EDF / EDF+ / BDF file reader -> a signal source for `fidetype live` (from the adapter template).

EDF (European Data Format, 16-bit) and BDF (BioSemi, 24-bit) are open, documented formats (https://www.edfplus.info/specs/). Many EEG, EMG and sleep systems export them. This reader is our own code (Apache-2.0), with no dependency beyond NumPy. It reads continuous files (EDF, EDF+C, BDF); EDF+D (discontinuous) raises `ValueError`. The `EDF/BDF Annotations` signal becomes markers. Samples are in physical units (`channel_units`: the file's physical dimension, for example `uV`).

Checked on real files: PhysioNet EEGMMIDB EDF+C (ODC-By 1.0) and the MNE-Python test EDF+C / BDF files (BSD-3-Clause) give the same values as MNE within one digital step (`tests/test_adapter_files_real.py`, local data only).

Privacy: the header fields "patient" and "recording" can hold personal data. The reader never copies them into `meta`.

### openbci-gui

Module `fidetype.adapters.openbci_gui`.

OpenBCI GUI recording reader -> a signal source for `fidetype live` (from the adapter template).

The OpenBCI GUI (v5 and later) saves a text file `OpenBCI-RAW-*.txt` (the sample files of the GUI: `OpenBCI_GUI-*.txt`): `%` header lines (`Sample Rate = 250 Hz`, `Board = ...`), one column-name line (`Sample Index, EXG Channel 0, ..., Timestamp, ...`) and one comma-separated row per sample. EXG values are microvolts. The reader keeps the EXG channels; a `Marker Channel` column (non-zero values) becomes markers. Times: the first `Timestamp` plus `(row + samples lost before the row) / sample_rate`. GUI v5 writes Unix seconds; the sample files of the GUI (v6 layout) write Unix milliseconds, so a first stamp above `1e11` is read as milliseconds. The packet stamps of the file are not used, because they repeat inside a packet. Older GUI files (v4 and before, no column-name line) raise `ValueError`.

**Packet drops.** On a Cyton board the `Sample Index` counts 0..255 and wraps (a wrap is not a drop). It steps by 1 (Cyton) or by 2 (Cyton + Daisy: one row per two radio packets). An index step `d` other than that is a drop of `((d - step) mod 256) / step` rows (the same index twice is an error, unless the stamps show one full cycle lost). If the `Timestamp` column shows that whole index cycles were lost too, they are added. `on_drop`:

- `"gap"` (default): keep every row. Rows after a drop get the correct later times, and the result lists the drops in `gaps` as `(row, missing_frames)`. `open_source` gives them to `fidetype.live.sources.ArraySource`, so the first chunk after a drop carries `gap` (LSL-G3 fields, `cause` = `"sample_index"`) and `fidetype live` cuts the open segment there (spec LSL-G2). - `"error"`: a drop raises `ValueError` (row and size in the message).

Other boards (Ganglion and others) have other index rules; their index is not checked (`index_checked` False). Real files read: the GUI sample file `OpenBCI_GUI-v6-blinks-jawClench-alpha.txt` (ms stamps), a Cyton GUI v5.0 file with 20 drops (seconds stamps) and a Cyton + Daisy GUI v5+ file with a `Marker Channel` (all zero). Our own code (Apache-2.0), NumPy only.
